title: Loss-of-function mutations in CFAP57 cause multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella in humans and mice.

reviewer.method: Entire main text read in sequential ranges 1–150,151–340,341–398 including references, endmatter and captions. All five main figure graphics and two tables inspected as pixels; all nine supplement pages read as text and pixels; all populated cells of four XLSX tables read. All 149 and 303 decoded movie frames inspected in sequential 480-pixel-wide contact sheets, plus native-resolution first frames. This is complete frame-image review, not continuous playback, tracking or independent CASA replication. Both distinct patient packets and all thirteen phenotype assertions checked individually.

audit.exposure_note: Post-inference audit with aggregate compact benchmark results seen; this case ranking not opened.

patient_identity.statement: P2 is Family1 IV:6, a 36-year-old infertile male, married 16 years.

evidence.locator: Results: identification of CFAP57 mutations; clinical characteristics; Methods WES and Sanger

genotype.statement: Figure 2B supports homozygous c.2872C>T/p.Arg958Ter in P2 and P3, matching the reported coding/protein substitution and allelic state.

evidence.locator: Results: identification of CFAP57 mutations; clinical characteristics; Methods WES and Sanger

limitations: Source uses NM_001195831.2 and hg19 chr1:43692660; packet uses NM_001378189.1 and hg38 chr1:43226989. Exact transcript/build equivalence has not been independently validated here.

segregation.statement: Both parents III:1 and III:2 are heterozygous; P2 and P3 are homozygous. Consanguinity and male phenotype support a recessive hypothesis.

evidence.locator: Results: identification of CFAP57 mutations; clinical characteristics; Methods WES and Sanger

limitations: The infertile female IV:3 is WT/WT: male infertility segregation must not be generalized to all infertility. P1 is not shown with a Sanger genotype.

phase.statement: Single candidate reported homozygous; two different alleles do not require cis/trans phasing. Parental heterozygosity supports recessive transmission.

evidence.locator: Results: identification of CFAP57 mutations; clinical characteristics; Methods WES and Sanger

limitations: Raw parental read data and orthogonal copy-number assessment are not supplied.

causal_confidence.statement: The source calls the CFAP57 mutations pathogenic using family/genetic and mouse evidence; it does not provide a formal ACMG classification table establishing the packet PATHOGENIC label.

Post-inference, aggregate-exposed source review; not a blinded clinical truth set.
Complete published-component review does not imply raw WES/CASA/Western data or independent assay replication.
Main Results calls DNAH10 a double-headed ODA marker, while Figure S6/S7 place it as double-headed IDA; this source wording discrepancy is retained.
Antibody epitope aa701–900 is absent from the short isoform, so the long-isoform antibody experiment does not directly establish short-isoform preservation.
No N1002K/BubR1 measurement, arimoclomol rescue or comparative therapeutic benefit is present in this paper.
